E-commerce at 1M, 10M and 100M requests/day: evolving Saga + Outbox by evidence

Turn a concrete e-commerce Saga + Outbox architecture into an evolution plan: preserve stock and payment correctness while search, cart, checkout, eventing and storage scale only when their own signals demand it.

Use the supplied e-commerce diagram as a logical target for a promotion: CDN and gateway at the edge; isolated search and cart paths; a durable Checkout Saga coordinating order, inventory and payment; and a local outbox beside each authoritative database. The image says 1M DAU and a 10x campaign, whereas this blueprint's shared yardstick is requests/day. Convert DAU into endpoint traffic before sizing anything, then decide what is one deploy at 1M requests/day, what splits at the 10M waypoint, and what only becomes justified near 100M or under an explicit blast-radius target. The skill is preserving the same business invariants while refusing distribution that has no measured constraint to remove.
Browse and search: Serve product images from the CDN, product details from cache or the catalog, and ranked results from a rebuildable search projection whose stock may be stale.
Cart: Persist the cart durably while using Redis only to accelerate active carts; an eviction or Redis outage must not erase a customer's order intent.
Checkout: Accept one idempotent checkout command, persist Saga state, create the order, reserve stock, process payment, then confirm or compensate each participant through explicit transitions.
After payment: Fan `PaymentCompleted` out to reviews, notification, analytics and search/index updates without placing those consumers on the checkout latency path.
Recovery: Expire abandoned reservations, reconcile `UNKNOWN` payments against the provider, replay outboxes, quarantine poison events and redrive the DLQ only after the consumer defect is fixed.
Stock invariant: Available stock never becomes negative, and at most one live reservation may consume the same scarce unit/version; search is not an authority for that decision.
Payment invariant: A client, gateway, Saga retry and provider webhook may all duplicate work, but one checkout intent can produce at most one captured amount under one provider idempotency key.
Local atomicity: Each service commits its state transition and outbox record in one local transaction; delivery and consumption remain duplicate-tolerant.
Failure isolation: Search, cart, payment and after-payment work use separate pools and bounded queues, so a slow PSP or review consumer cannot exhaust checkout or browse capacity.
Operability: Alert on aged Saga states, outbox age, consumer lag, DLQ growth, reserve conflicts, payment `UNKNOWN` age and reconciliation mismatches rather than CPU alone.

Unit guard: 1M DAU is not requests/day. Estimate `requests/day = DAU × journeys/user/day × API calls/journey`, then split by browse, cart and checkout endpoint; report the assumptions beside the result.

1M request scale: 1M requests/day is 11.6 rps average and about 250 rps peak under the site's 20x planning factor. One relational primary and one coarse application deployment may still be enough; preserve the logical ownership shown in the image without paying for a database and on-call team per box.

10M waypoint: 10M requests/day is 116 rps average and about 2,500 rps peak. A 10x promotion is a burst profile, not automatically 10M/day: measure its duration, endpoint mix, cache-hit ratio and hot-SKU skew, then cap accepted checkout work to the inventory and PSP drain rates.

Write amplification: One accepted checkout can create order, reservation and payment writes plus several outbox, inbox and derived-index records. Size database IOPS, WAL, broker ingress and consumers from commands and events per checkout, not from the public API count alone.

Serialized hot key: Ten stateless inventory replicas do not raise the safe rate for one SKU row or one ordered partition. Benchmark that critical section, reserve headroom, and use per-SKU admission or a waiting room when demand exceeds its drain rate.

100M scale: About 25,000 rps peak is a fleet-sizing number. Introduce shards or cells only for measured write/data volume, restore-time or blast-radius limits; model it as roughly ten independently operable T3-to-waypoint cells rather than one giant shared checkout.
Critical checkout commands, local outboxes and asynchronous effects

Product and search document — Product DB is authoritative for catalog data; Elasticsearch/OpenSearch is a denormalized projection with `source_version` and `indexed_at`, so it can be stale, discarded and rebuilt.
Cart — Durable cart rows own product, quantity and price-snapshot references; Cart Redis is a TTL acceleration tier for active sessions, never the only copy of checkout intent.

Checkout request and Saga — `idempotency_key`, canonical request hash, original response, Saga state, step attempts, deadlines and version. Keep request dedupe with the transaction that creates the Saga, not in an eventually consistent global cache.
Order — One aggregate with legal `CREATED → CONFIRMED | CANCELLED` transitions and a version. Order Service alone changes it; the Saga requests transitions but never writes Order DB directly.

Inventory reservation — `sku_id`, quantity, order id, expiry, state and fencing version. A conditional update or uniqueness constraint is the final oversell guard; Redis may protect capacity but not replace this invariant.

Payment attempt — Amount, currency, order id, provider idempotency key/reference and explicit `PENDING | SUCCEEDED | FAILED | UNKNOWN | REFUNDED` states. Timeout means query and reconcile, not retry with a new key.

Outbox and inbox — Stable event/command id, aggregate id, aggregate version, type, payload and occurred time. Outbox closes the database/broker dual-write gap; inbox or an effect-specific unique key makes at-least-once delivery harmless.

Image CDN — Problem solved: remove large immutable image and static-file reads from application compute and origin bandwidth. Flow position: App/Web requests a content-addressed URL such as `products/42/sha256.webp` directly from the nearest edge; business APIs still enter the gateway. Failure / cost: a bad cache key serves stale content, an expiry wave stampedes the origin, and public caching can leak private responses; use versioned URLs, long immutable TTLs, origin shielding and a placeholder when the CDN is unavailable. Tier verdict: 1M worth it; 10M mandatory for image-heavy browse; 100M needs its own scaling story across regions and origins.

API Gateway — Problem solved: give clients one stable edge contract for TLS termination, authentication hand-off, coarse authorization, routing, request-size limits and per-route rate limits. Flow position: every dynamic `/search`, `/cart` and `/checkout` call enters here, receives a correlation id and is routed to an independently budgeted backend pool. Failure / cost: it is a high-blast-radius choke point; policy mistakes reject all traffic, retries can amplify overload, and deep business authorization here becomes unmaintainable. Run multiple instances across zones, fail closed for auth, return explicit `429` with backoff, and keep domain checks in services. Tier verdict: 1M worth it; 10M mandatory; 100M needs its own scaling story per cell or region.

Service discovery with Kubernetes Service/DNS — Problem solved: let gateway and services call a stable name while Pods and IPs are replaced. Flow position: `checkout.default.svc.cluster.local` resolves to a Service whose EndpointSlices track healthy checkout replicas; clients still need connection timeouts, load balancing and readiness because DNS only finds an endpoint. Failure / cost: stale DNS caches, an unhealthy readiness probe or a control-plane outage can route poorly, while a second custom registry duplicates platform state. Tier verdict: platform discovery is 1M worth it and 10M mandatory once replicas move; a custom registry is not needed at either tier; 100M cross-cell discovery needs its own scaling story.

Search Service plus Elasticsearch/OpenSearch — Problem solved: full-text relevance, typo tolerance, filtering, faceting and sorting that a transactional Product DB should not execute on every browse request. Flow position: product and stock events update a versioned `products-v42` projection; Search Service queries it and returns `source_version` or `indexed_at`, while checkout revalidates stock in Inventory. Failure / cost: refresh and consumer lag make results stale, mappings and shard counts are expensive to change, hot queries exhaust heap, and out-of-order events can overwrite newer documents; reject older source versions and keep a rebuild path from Product DB/outbox. Tier verdict: 1M worth it when product search is real; 10M mandatory for the depicted search-heavy lane; 100M needs its own scaling story for shards, indexing and relevance.

Product Redis cache — Problem solved: absorb repeated product-detail reads and protect Product DB connection/IO budgets. Flow position: Search or Product Service performs cache-aside `GET product:{id}:v{source_version}`, loads the authoritative row on a miss, then `SET`s a bounded TTL; writes commit to Product DB first and invalidate or advance the versioned key. Failure / cost: stale values, eviction and Redis outage are expected; simultaneous misses create a stampede and one hot key can saturate a shard, so use single-flight fill, jittered TTL, negative caching with a short TTL and a direct-to-origin concurrency cap. Tier verdict: 1M worth it; 10M mandatory for the hot catalogue path shown; 100M needs its own scaling story for memory, hot keys and failover.

Cart DB plus Cart Redis — Problem solved: Cart DB preserves customer intent across sessions, while Redis reduces latency for repeatedly edited active carts. Flow position: Cart Service writes the durable cart with an optimistic version and may cache `cart:{customer_id}`; checkout always reloads or validates the durable version and current price/stock rules. Failure / cost: cache eviction must become a miss, never an empty cart; dual writes can diverge, long TTLs expose stale quantity and a hot anonymous campaign can consume memory. Prefer database-first plus invalidate, measure hit rate and cap cart size. Tier verdict: durable Cart DB is 1M mandatory; Cart Redis is 1M not needed, 10M worth it, and 100M needs its own scaling story.

Checkout Saga plus Checkout DB — Problem solved: preserve progress across the Order, Inventory and Payment transaction boundaries when no single ACID commit covers them. Flow position: Checkout persists `RECEIVED → STOCK_HELD → PAYMENT_PENDING → CONFIRMED`, deadlines and step attempts before issuing idempotent participant commands; workers can restart from durable state and compensations are explicit new commands. Failure / cost: the orchestrator couples workflow knowledge, can become a control-plane hotspot, and compensation may fail or be semantically impossible after an external effect. Partition workers by checkout/order id, fence concurrent transitions and reconcile aged non-terminal rows. Tier verdict: 1M not needed while all participants share one local transaction; 10M mandatory only after they become separate authorities; 100M needs its own scaling story per cell.

Idempotency store — Problem solved: make client retries, gateway retries and duplicate submissions return one logical checkout outcome. Flow position: the transaction that creates the Saga inserts `(tenant, idempotency_key, canonical_request_hash, status, original_response)` under a unique constraint; the same key with a different hash is rejected, while an exact replay returns the stored response. Failure / cost: a remote eventually consistent cache allows races, unbounded retention grows forever, and deleting keys too early reopens duplicate capture risk. Co-locate it with Checkout DB, define retention from the longest retry/webhook window and monitor hot keys. Tier verdict: 1M mandatory; 10M mandatory; 100M needs its own scaling story for partitioning and retention.

Order Service plus relational Order DB — Problem solved: own the legal order lifecycle and audit trail independently of the Saga's opinion. Flow position: idempotent `Create`, `Confirm` and `Cancel` commands perform conditional transitions such as `CREATED → CONFIRMED | CANCELLED`, then record an outbox event in the same transaction; no other service writes Order tables. Failure / cost: cross-service joins disappear, stale commands conflict by version, and premature service/database separation adds network and on-call cost. Keep indexes around customer/status/time and archive by policy rather than sharding the headline. Tier verdict: the relational state machine is 1M mandatory; a separate service/database is 1M not needed, 10M worth it for ownership/isolation, and 100M needs its own scaling story.

Inventory Service plus relational Inventory DB — Problem solved: make stock reservation the single authority that prevents oversell. Flow position: `Reserve(sku, qty, order)` performs one short conditional update such as `available >= qty AND version = expected`, inserts an expiring reservation and outbox row, then `Confirm` or `Release` transitions that exact reservation idempotently. Failure / cost: one promotional SKU remains a serialized hot key even with many replicas; lock waits, expired holds and duplicate release commands must be visible. Use a database constraint as the final guard, admission/waiting-room controls for the hot SKU and reconciliation for leaked reservations. Tier verdict: the invariant is 1M mandatory and 10M mandatory; 100M needs its own scaling story by SKU/warehouse, not random request sharding.

Payment Service plus relational Payment DB — Problem solved: isolate provider-specific APIs while keeping one authoritative payment-attempt ledger. Flow position: it stores amount, currency, order id, provider reference and one reused provider idempotency key, calls the PSP outside the database transaction, records webhook/status-query evidence, and emits a local outbox event. Failure / cost: timeout means `UNKNOWN`, not failed; retrying with a fresh key may double-charge, late success may require refund, and a slow PSP can exhaust checkout workers. Use strict timeouts, a separate concurrency budget, status polling/webhooks and financial reconciliation. Tier verdict: durable attempts and idempotency are 1M mandatory; provider isolation is 10M worth it; 100M needs its own scaling story per provider/region.

Transactional Outbox, relay and consumer Inbox — Problem solved: close the database/broker dual-write gap without a distributed transaction. Flow position: each Order, Inventory or Payment transaction appends a stable event id and aggregate version locally; a relay publishes unprocessed rows, and each consumer records the event id plus its side effect in one local transaction. Failure / cost: a relay crash after publish causes duplicates, backlog grows the source DB, and out-of-order delivery can apply stale state; therefore publication is at-least-once, not end-to-end exactly-once. Monitor oldest outbox age, batch with `SKIP LOCKED`, deduplicate and reject stale versions. Tier verdict: 1M not needed while one local transaction has no broker side effect; 10M mandatory for the depicted split; 100M needs its own scaling story for relay throughput and retention.

Kafka event log — Problem solved: retain replayable domain events and let checkout, search, analytics and after-payment consumer groups advance independently. Flow position: outbox relays publish `OrderCreated`, `StockReserved` and `PaymentCompleted` keyed by the aggregate whose order matters; one partition preserves order for that key and each group gets its own copy. Failure / cost: consumers can replay duplicates, rebalances pause work, retention can remove repair history, and adding partitions changes key distribution while one hot key still cannot use several partitions. Size partitions from measured bytes/events, use schemas and compatibility checks, and alert on oldest lag rather than broker CPU alone. Tier verdict: 1M worth it when replay or multiple groups are required; 10M mandatory for the pictured fan-out; 100M needs its own scaling story for partitions, storage and cross-cell replication.

RabbitMQ work queues — Problem solved: route one command or task to one logical worker with broker-side acknowledgements, redelivery and queue-level policies. Flow position: it can carry fulfilment, email or compensation commands whose consumer acknowledges only after its local effect commits; publisher confirms cover broker acceptance, not consumer success. Failure / cost: redelivery is at-least-once, requeue loops can burn capacity, a queue can become a single ordered bottleneck, and RabbitMQ is not Kafka-style retained replay by default. Set prefetch/concurrency budgets, durable or quorum queues where required, idempotent handlers and policy-managed dead lettering. Tier verdict: 1M not needed when direct calls or Kafka events suffice; 10M worth it for routed work; if selected at 100M it needs its own scaling story.

Bounded retry plus DLQ — Problem solved: recover transient delivery/dependency failures without one poison record blocking a partition or queue forever. Flow position: the consumer retries only classified transient errors with exponential backoff and jitter, then parks the original payload, headers, schema version and failure reason in quarantine; an owner fixes the defect and explicitly redrives it. Failure / cost: retry amplifies outages, delayed work can violate business deadlines, and a DLQ is not automatic repair or an archive. Cap attempts and elapsed time, preserve ordering requirements, alert on oldest age/growth and reconcile before redrive. Tier verdict: 1M mandatory for any asynchronous lane; 10M mandatory; 100M needs its own scaling story for quarantine volume and operator tooling.

After-payment workers and After Payment DB — Problem solved: keep reviews, notifications, analytics and other non-critical effects off checkout latency while allowing each to lag or replay independently. Flow position: dedicated consumer groups process `PaymentCompleted`, write their own local state with an inbox/effect unique key and expose completion separately from the order's authoritative payment state. Failure / cost: users may see delayed email/review eligibility, fan-out multiplies event traffic, and one consumer's schema bug can accumulate a large backlog. Give every effect an SLO, concurrency budget, retention/rebuild plan and owner; never let its outage reject a paid order. Tier verdict: 1M worth it; 10M mandatory for failure isolation; 100M needs its own scaling story per consumer domain.

Observability and reconciliation workers — Problem solved: detect and repair ambiguous distributed state that metrics on HTTP success cannot prove correct. Flow position: traces carry checkout/order/event ids, dashboards join accepted-to-completed ratio with oldest Saga/outbox/consumer age, and scheduled reconcilers compare Checkout, Order, Inventory, Payment and PSP evidence before issuing explicit confirm/release/cancel/refund repairs. Failure / cost: high-cardinality telemetry is expensive, sampling can hide rare money errors, and an unsafe repair job can magnify corruption. Keep immutable audit evidence, dry-run repair plans and require idempotent, fenced transitions. Tier verdict: 1M mandatory; 10M mandatory; at 100M the telemetry and repair plane needs its own scaling story.

Shards and cells — Problem solved: bound dataset/restore time, write contention and regional blast radius after simpler tuning is exhausted. Flow position: a versioned router keeps Checkout, Order and Payment for one order in one cell, while Inventory remains routed by its SKU/warehouse authority; migrations copy, stream ordered changes, verify invariants, cut one range over and fence the old writer. Failure / cost: cross-cell workflows, routing-map mistakes, skew, rebalancing and duplicated platform/on-call estates are permanent complexity; independent dual writes are not a migration strategy. Tier verdict: 1M not needed; 10M not needed unless measured restore or blast-radius targets say otherwise; at 100M it needs its own scaling story and is mandatory only when those targets require it.

Logical architecture versus operational estate — The picture is an excellent ownership map but an expensive day-one deployment. Keeping boxes logical at 1M preserves simple transactions and on-call; splitting the measured hot lanes at 10M buys isolation while adding network failure, versioned contracts and more deployments.

Orchestration versus choreography — Checkout Saga makes sequence, timeout and compensation visible in one place. It also becomes a control-plane hotspot and coupling point; persist state, partition workers and keep participant APIs idempotent so losing the orchestrator process loses no workflow.

Asynchronous checkout — Moving payment status and secondary effects behind the broker bounds request latency and isolates dependencies. Users now need a truthful `PENDING` contract, while operators own backlog age, replay, DLQ and workflows that can remain incomplete for hours.

Compensation is not rollback — Releasing inventory, cancelling an order or refunding a payment is a new business action that may fail after the original action became externally visible. Every compensation needs its own idempotency, legal precondition, audit record and reconciliation fallback.

Outbox guarantee — The local database change and outbox row are atomic, but publication can repeat and consumers can crash after their side effect. Stable event ids, aggregate sequence checks and inbox/effect uniqueness are permanent costs of the reliability gained.

Database per service — Ownership and failure isolation improve, but joins, reports and cross-domain consistency become asynchronous products. Do not let the Saga update another service's tables, and build analytics from events/CDC rather than cross-service request-time joins.

Adoption order — Tune query/index and pools, isolate browse from checkout, add CDN/cache and asynchronous secondary effects, then partition consumers and only later shard/cell. Each step needs a triggering metric, owner, rollback and failure drill; otherwise the architecture can only grow.
Which invariant can break?

Oversell, duplicate capture and an order marked confirmed while stock or payment disagrees are the critical failures. Inventory conditional updates, one provider idempotency key and legal versioned transitions in each authoritative service guard them; the Saga coordinates but is not the source of truth for participant state.
Which metric detects it first?

Watch accepted-to-completed checkout ratio and p99 together with oldest non-terminal Saga age, outbox age, consumer lag, reserve-conflict rate, PSP `UNKNOWN` age and reconciliation mismatches. Queue depth alone hides a stalled partition.
How is blast radius contained?

Use separate gateway routes, pools, concurrency budgets and bounded queues for browse, cart, checkout, PSP and after-payment lanes. Partition by order/SKU as required, cap one campaign or hot SKU at admission, and let secondary consumers lag without consuming checkout capacity.
Can retry duplicate or reorder work?

Yes by default. Bind the client key to a canonical request hash and original response, reuse the same provider key, assign every command/event a stable id plus aggregate version, and apply each consumer effect in a local transaction with an inbox or unique business key.
How do we repair and prove recovery?

Reconcile aged Saga rows against Order, Inventory, Payment and the PSP; replay committed outboxes; repair by explicit confirm, release, cancel or refund transitions; then redrive quarantined events. Prove recovery with zero unmatched captures/reservations, bounded outbox and consumer age, and sampled aggregate sequence checks.

E-commerce ở 1M, 10M và 100M requests/day: tiến hoá Saga + Outbox theo bằng chứng
Biến một kiến trúc e-commerce Saga + Outbox cụ thể thành evolution plan: giữ đúng stock/payment trong khi search, cart, checkout, eventing và storage chỉ scale khi signal riêng của chúng đòi hỏi.

Dùng sơ đồ e-commerce được cung cấp làm logical target cho promotion: CDN và gateway ở edge; search/cart path cô lập; Checkout Saga bền vững điều phối order, inventory và payment; mỗi authoritative database có local outbox. Ảnh ghi 1M DAU và campaign 10x, còn yardstick chung của blueprint là requests/day. Phải quy DAU thành traffic theo endpoint trước khi size, rồi quyết định phần nào vẫn chung một deployment ở 1M requests/day, phần nào tách tại waypoint 10M, và phần nào chỉ hợp lý gần 100M hoặc khi có blast-radius target rõ ràng. Skill cốt lõi là giữ nguyên business invariant nhưng từ chối distribution không gỡ một measured constraint nào.
Browse và search: Serve product image từ CDN, product detail từ cache/catalog và ranked result từ search projection rebuild được; stock trên projection được phép stale.
Cart: Persist cart bền vững, chỉ dùng Redis để tăng tốc active cart; eviction hoặc Redis outage không được xoá order intent của khách.
Checkout: Nhận một checkout command idempotent, persist Saga state, tạo order, reserve stock, xử lý payment rồi confirm hoặc compensate từng participant bằng transition tường minh.
After payment: Fan `PaymentCompleted` sang review, notification, analytics và search/index update mà không đặt các consumer này trên checkout latency path.
Recovery: Expire reservation bị bỏ, reconcile payment `UNKNOWN` với provider, replay outbox, quarantine poison event và chỉ redrive DLQ sau khi đã sửa consumer defect.
Stock invariant: Available stock không âm và tối đa một live reservation được consume cùng scarce unit/version; search không có authority cho quyết định đó.
Payment invariant: Client, gateway, Saga retry và provider webhook đều có thể duplicate work, nhưng một checkout intent chỉ tạo tối đa một captured amount dưới cùng provider idempotency key.
Local atomicity: Mỗi service commit state transition và outbox record trong một local transaction; delivery và consumption vẫn phải chịu được duplicate.
Failure isolation: Search, cart, payment và after-payment dùng pool cùng bounded queue riêng để PSP chậm hay review consumer lỗi không làm cạn checkout/browse capacity.
Operability: Alert theo Saga state quá tuổi, outbox age, consumer lag, DLQ growth, reserve conflict, tuổi payment `UNKNOWN` và reconciliation mismatch thay vì chỉ CPU.
Unit guard: 1M DAU không phải requests/day. Ước lượng `requests/day = DAU × journeys/user/day × API calls/journey`, rồi tách theo endpoint browse, cart và checkout; ghi assumption cạnh kết quả.

Scale 1M request: 1M requests/day là 11,6 rps average và khoảng 250 rps peak theo planning factor 20x của site. Một relational primary và coarse application deployment có thể vẫn đủ; giữ logical ownership trong ảnh mà chưa phải trả giá một database và on-call team cho mỗi box.

Waypoint 10M: 10M requests/day là 116 rps average và khoảng 2.500 rps peak. Promotion 10x là burst profile, không tự động thành 10M/day: phải đo duration, endpoint mix, cache-hit ratio và hot-SKU skew, rồi cap checkout accepted theo drain rate của inventory và PSP.

Write amplification: Một checkout accepted có thể tạo write cho order, reservation, payment cùng nhiều outbox, inbox và derived-index record. Size database IOPS, WAL, broker ingress và consumer từ command/event trên mỗi checkout, không chỉ public API count.

Serialized hot key: Mười inventory replica stateless không nâng safe rate của một SKU row hoặc một ordered partition. Benchmark critical section đó, chừa headroom và dùng admission/waiting room theo SKU khi demand vượt drain rate.

Scale 100M: Khoảng 25.000 rps peak là số để size fleet. Chỉ thêm shard/cell khi write/data volume, restore time hoặc blast radius đã đo bị chặn; model thành khoảng mười cell vận hành độc lập ở mức T3-to-waypoint thay vì một checkout khổng lồ dùng chung.
Checkout command quan trọng, local outbox và effect bất đồng bộ
Product và search document — Product DB authoritative cho catalog; Elasticsearch/OpenSearch là denormalized projection có `source_version` và `indexed_at`, nên được phép stale, xoá và rebuild.
Cart — Durable cart row sở hữu product, quantity và price-snapshot reference; Cart Redis là TTL acceleration tier cho active session, không bao giờ là bản duy nhất của checkout intent.

Checkout request và Saga — `idempotency_key`, canonical request hash, original response, Saga state, step attempt, deadline và version. Đặt request dedupe cạnh transaction tạo Saga, không đặt trong global cache eventual.
Order — Một aggregate với transition hợp lệ `CREATED → CONFIRMED | CANCELLED` và version. Chỉ Order Service được đổi nó; Saga yêu cầu transition nhưng không bao giờ write thẳng Order DB.

Inventory reservation — `sku_id`, quantity, order id, expiry, state và fencing version. Conditional update hoặc unique constraint là oversell guard cuối; Redis được bảo vệ capacity nhưng không thay invariant này.

Payment attempt — Amount, currency, order id, provider idempotency key/reference và state rõ `PENDING | SUCCEEDED | FAILED | UNKNOWN | REFUNDED`. Timeout nghĩa là query/reconcile, không retry bằng key mới.

Outbox và inbox — Stable event/command id, aggregate id, aggregate version, type, payload và occurred time. Outbox đóng gap dual-write database/broker; inbox hoặc effect-specific unique key làm at-least-once delivery trở nên vô hại.

Image CDN — Vấn đề giải quyết: kéo các lượt đọc image/static file lớn, immutable ra khỏi application compute và origin bandwidth. Vị trí trong flow: App/Web lấy content-addressed URL như `products/42/sha256.webp` trực tiếp từ edge gần nhất; business API vẫn đi vào gateway. Failure / cái giá: cache key sai phục vụ nội dung cũ, một đợt expiry đồng loạt stampede origin, còn public cache có thể làm lộ private response; dùng versioned URL, immutable TTL dài, origin shielding và placeholder khi CDN unavailable. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M nên có; 10M bắt buộc cho browse nặng ảnh; 100M cần scale riêng theo region và origin.

API Gateway — Vấn đề giải quyết: cho client một edge contract ổn định để terminate TLS, hand-off authentication, coarse authorization, route, giới hạn request size và rate-limit theo route. Vị trí trong flow: mọi dynamic call `/search`, `/cart`, `/checkout` vào đây, nhận correlation id rồi được route sang backend pool có budget độc lập. Failure / cái giá: đây là choke point có blast radius lớn; policy sai reject toàn traffic, retry khuếch đại overload, còn nhét domain authorization sâu vào gateway sẽ khó bảo trì. Chạy nhiều instance đa zone, fail closed cho auth, trả `429` kèm backoff và giữ domain check trong service. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M nên có; 10M bắt buộc; 100M cần scale riêng theo cell hoặc region.

Service discovery bằng Kubernetes Service/DNS — Vấn đề giải quyết: cho gateway/service gọi một tên ổn định trong khi Pod và IP liên tục bị thay. Vị trí trong flow: `checkout.default.svc.cluster.local` resolve tới Service có EndpointSlice theo dõi checkout replica healthy; client vẫn cần connection timeout, load balancing và readiness vì DNS chỉ tìm endpoint. Failure / cái giá: DNS cache cũ, readiness probe sai hoặc control-plane outage có thể route tệ, còn custom registry thứ hai sẽ duplicate platform state. Phán quyết theo tier: platform discovery ở 1M nên có và 10M bắt buộc khi replica di chuyển; custom registry không cần ở cả hai tier; discovery cross-cell ở 100M cần scale riêng.

Search Service plus Elasticsearch/OpenSearch — Vấn đề giải quyết: full-text relevance, typo tolerance, filter, facet và sort mà transactional Product DB không nên chạy cho mọi browse request. Vị trí trong flow: product/stock event cập nhật projection versioned `products-v42`; Search Service query nó và trả `source_version` hoặc `indexed_at`, còn checkout revalidate stock tại Inventory. Failure / cái giá: refresh cùng consumer lag làm kết quả stale, mapping/shard count đắt để đổi, hot query làm cạn heap, còn event out-of-order có thể ghi đè document mới; reject source version cũ và giữ đường rebuild từ Product DB/outbox. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M nên có khi sản phẩm thật sự cần search; 10M bắt buộc cho search-heavy lane trong hình; 100M cần scale riêng cho shard, indexing và relevance.

Product Redis cache — Vấn đề giải quyết: hấp thụ product-detail read lặp lại và bảo vệ connection/IO budget của Product DB. Vị trí trong flow: Search hoặc Product Service chạy cache-aside `GET product:{id}:v{source_version}`, load authoritative row khi miss rồi `SET` với TTL hữu hạn; write commit Product DB trước rồi invalidate hoặc tăng versioned key. Failure / cái giá: stale value, eviction và Redis outage là trạng thái phải dự kiến; miss đồng thời tạo stampede, một hot key có thể bão hoà shard, nên dùng single-flight fill, TTL có jitter, negative cache TTL ngắn và direct-to-origin concurrency cap. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M nên có; 10M bắt buộc cho hot catalogue path trong hình; 100M cần scale riêng cho memory, hot key và failover.

Cart DB plus Cart Redis — Vấn đề giải quyết: Cart DB giữ customer intent qua nhiều session, còn Redis giảm latency cho active cart bị sửa liên tục. Vị trí trong flow: Cart Service ghi durable cart kèm optimistic version và có thể cache `cart:{customer_id}`; checkout luôn reload hoặc validate durable version cùng rule price/stock hiện tại. Failure / cái giá: cache eviction phải thành miss, không được thành empty cart; dual write có thể lệch, TTL dài lộ quantity cũ, còn campaign nhiều anonymous cart ngốn memory. Ưu tiên database-first rồi invalidate, đo hit rate và cap cart size. Phán quyết theo tier: durable Cart DB ở 1M bắt buộc; Cart Redis ở 1M không cần, 10M nên có và 100M cần scale riêng.

Checkout Saga plus Checkout DB — Vấn đề giải quyết: giữ tiến độ qua transaction boundary Order, Inventory và Payment khi không có một ACID commit bao phủ tất cả. Vị trí trong flow: Checkout persist `RECEIVED → STOCK_HELD → PAYMENT_PENDING → CONFIRMED`, deadline và step attempt trước khi phát idempotent command; worker restart được từ durable state, còn compensation là command mới tường minh. Failure / cái giá: orchestrator gom workflow knowledge, có thể thành control-plane hotspot, còn compensation có thể fail hoặc không còn ý nghĩa sau external effect. Partition worker theo checkout/order id, fence concurrent transition và reconcile non-terminal row quá tuổi. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M không cần khi mọi participant còn chung một local transaction; 10M bắt buộc chỉ sau khi chúng thành authority tách biệt; 100M cần scale riêng theo cell.

Idempotency store — Vấn đề giải quyết: biến client retry, gateway retry và submit trùng thành một logical checkout outcome. Vị trí trong flow: transaction tạo Saga insert `(tenant, idempotency_key, canonical_request_hash, status, original_response)` dưới unique constraint; cùng key nhưng hash khác bị reject, còn replay đúng trả stored response. Failure / cái giá: remote cache eventually consistent cho phép race, retention vô hạn phình mãi, còn xoá key quá sớm mở lại rủi ro capture trùng. Co-locate với Checkout DB, đặt retention theo retry/webhook window dài nhất và monitor hot key. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M bắt buộc; 10M bắt buộc; 100M cần scale riêng cho partitioning và retention.

Order Service plus relational Order DB — Vấn đề giải quyết: sở hữu legal order lifecycle và audit trail độc lập với ý kiến của Saga. Vị trí trong flow: idempotent command `Create`, `Confirm`, `Cancel` chạy conditional transition như `CREATED → CONFIRMED | CANCELLED`, rồi ghi outbox event trong cùng transaction; không service nào khác viết Order table. Failure / cái giá: cross-service join biến mất, command stale conflict theo version, còn tách service/database quá sớm thêm network và on-call cost. Giữ index quanh customer/status/time và archive theo policy thay vì shard theo headline. Phán quyết theo tier: relational state machine ở 1M bắt buộc; service/database riêng ở 1M không cần, 10M nên có vì ownership/isolation và 100M cần scale riêng.

Inventory Service plus relational Inventory DB — Vấn đề giải quyết: biến stock reservation thành authority duy nhất chống oversell. Vị trí trong flow: `Reserve(sku, qty, order)` chạy một conditional update ngắn như `available >= qty AND version = expected`, insert reservation có expiry cùng outbox row, rồi `Confirm` hoặc `Release` đúng reservation đó theo cách idempotent. Failure / cái giá: một promotional SKU vẫn là serialized hot key dù có nhiều replica; lock wait, hold hết hạn và release command trùng phải quan sát được. Dùng database constraint làm guard cuối, admission/waiting room cho hot SKU và reconciliation cho reservation rò rỉ. Phán quyết theo tier: invariant ở 1M bắt buộc và 10M bắt buộc; 100M cần scale riêng theo SKU/warehouse, không random-shard request.

Payment Service plus relational Payment DB — Vấn đề giải quyết: cô lập provider-specific API trong khi giữ một payment-attempt ledger authoritative. Vị trí trong flow: service lưu amount, currency, order id, provider reference và một provider idempotency key được tái dùng, gọi PSP ngoài database transaction, ghi evidence từ webhook/status query rồi phát local outbox event. Failure / cái giá: timeout nghĩa là `UNKNOWN`, không phải failed; retry bằng key mới có thể double-charge, late success có thể phải refund, còn PSP chậm làm cạn checkout worker. Dùng strict timeout, concurrency budget riêng, status polling/webhook và financial reconciliation. Phán quyết theo tier: durable attempt cùng idempotency ở 1M bắt buộc; provider isolation ở 10M nên có; 100M cần scale riêng theo provider/region.

Transactional Outbox, relay và consumer Inbox — Vấn đề giải quyết: đóng database/broker dual-write gap mà không cần distributed transaction. Vị trí trong flow: mỗi transaction Order, Inventory hoặc Payment append stable event id cùng aggregate version ở local; relay publish row chưa xử lý, còn consumer ghi event id cùng side effect trong một local transaction. Failure / cái giá: relay crash sau publish tạo duplicate, backlog làm source DB lớn dần, delivery out-of-order có thể apply state cũ; vì vậy publication là at-least-once, không phải exactly-once end-to-end. Monitor oldest outbox age, batch bằng `SKIP LOCKED`, deduplicate và reject stale version. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M không cần khi một local transaction chưa có broker side effect; 10M bắt buộc cho shape tách trong hình; 100M cần scale riêng cho relay throughput và retention.

Kafka event log — Vấn đề giải quyết: giữ domain event replayable và cho consumer group checkout, search, analytics, after-payment tiến độc lập. Vị trí trong flow: outbox relay publish `OrderCreated`, `StockReserved`, `PaymentCompleted` với key là aggregate cần ordering; một partition giữ thứ tự cho key đó và mỗi group nhận bản riêng. Failure / cái giá: consumer có thể replay duplicate, rebalance tạm dừng xử lý, retention có thể xoá repair history, thêm partition đổi key distribution trong khi một hot key vẫn không dùng được nhiều partition. Size partition từ bytes/events đã đo, dùng schema/compatibility check và alert oldest lag thay vì chỉ broker CPU. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M nên có khi cần replay hoặc nhiều group; 10M bắt buộc cho fan-out trong hình; 100M cần scale riêng cho partition, storage và cross-cell replication.

RabbitMQ work queue — Vấn đề giải quyết: route một command/task tới một logical worker bằng broker acknowledgement, redelivery và queue policy. Vị trí trong flow: có thể chở fulfilment, email hoặc compensation command; consumer chỉ ack sau khi local effect commit, còn publisher confirm chỉ chứng minh broker nhận chứ không chứng minh consumer thành công. Failure / cái giá: redelivery là at-least-once, requeue loop đốt capacity, một queue có thể thành ordered bottleneck, còn RabbitMQ mặc định không phải retained replay kiểu Kafka. Đặt prefetch/concurrency budget, dùng durable hoặc quorum queue khi cần, handler idempotent và dead lettering quản lý bằng policy. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M không cần khi direct call hoặc Kafka event đã đủ; 10M nên có cho routed work; nếu chọn ở 100M thì cần scale riêng.

Bounded retry plus DLQ — Vấn đề giải quyết: phục hồi transient delivery/dependency failure mà không để một poison record chặn partition hoặc queue mãi. Vị trí trong flow: consumer chỉ retry lỗi transient đã classify với exponential backoff plus jitter, sau đó park original payload, header, schema version và failure reason vào quarantine; owner sửa defect rồi redrive tường minh. Failure / cái giá: retry khuếch đại outage, work trễ có thể vi phạm business deadline, còn DLQ không phải automatic repair hay archive. Giới hạn attempt cùng elapsed time, giữ ordering requirement, alert oldest age/growth và reconcile trước redrive. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M bắt buộc cho mọi async lane; 10M bắt buộc; 100M cần scale riêng cho quarantine volume và operator tooling.

After-payment worker và After Payment DB — Vấn đề giải quyết: đưa review, notification, analytics cùng non-critical effect ra khỏi checkout latency, cho từng consumer lag/replay độc lập. Vị trí trong flow: consumer group riêng xử lý `PaymentCompleted`, ghi local state bằng inbox/effect unique key và expose completion tách khỏi authoritative payment state của order. Failure / cái giá: user có thể nhận email/review eligibility trễ, fan-out nhân event traffic, còn schema bug của một consumer tạo backlog lớn. Mỗi effect cần SLO, concurrency budget, retention/rebuild plan và owner; outage của nó không bao giờ được reject paid order. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M nên có; 10M bắt buộc để failure isolation; 100M cần scale riêng theo consumer domain.

Observability và reconciliation worker — Vấn đề giải quyết: detect/repair distributed state mơ hồ mà HTTP success metric không thể chứng minh đúng. Vị trí trong flow: trace mang checkout/order/event id, dashboard ghép accepted-to-completed ratio với oldest Saga/outbox/consumer age, còn scheduled reconciler so Checkout, Order, Inventory, Payment và PSP evidence trước khi phát confirm/release/cancel/refund repair tường minh. Failure / cái giá: telemetry high-cardinality đắt, sampling có thể che money error hiếm, còn repair job không an toàn khuếch đại corruption. Giữ audit evidence immutable, dry-run repair plan và bắt buộc transition idempotent có fencing. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M bắt buộc; 10M bắt buộc; ở 100M telemetry/repair plane cần scale riêng.

Shard và cell — Vấn đề giải quyết: giới hạn dataset/restore time, write contention và regional blast radius sau khi tuning đơn giản đã hết hiệu lực. Vị trí trong flow: versioned router giữ Checkout, Order, Payment của một order trong cùng cell, còn Inventory vẫn route theo authority SKU/warehouse; migration copy, stream ordered change, verify invariant, cutover từng range rồi fence writer cũ. Failure / cái giá: cross-cell workflow, routing-map bug, skew, rebalance cùng platform/on-call estate bị nhân là complexity vĩnh viễn; independent dual write không phải migration strategy. Phán quyết theo tier: 1M không cần; 10M không cần trừ khi measured restore/blast-radius target nói khác; ở 100M cần scale riêng và chỉ bắt buộc khi các target đó đòi hỏi.

Logical architecture versus operational estate — Ảnh là ownership map rất tốt nhưng là day-one deployment đắt. Giữ box ở mức logical tại 1M giúp transaction/on-call đơn giản; tách hot lane đã đo ở 10M mua isolation nhưng thêm network failure, versioned contract và deployment.

Orchestration versus choreography — Checkout Saga làm sequence, timeout và compensation nhìn thấy ở một chỗ. Nó cũng thành control-plane hotspot/coupling point; phải persist state, partition worker và giữ participant API idempotent để mất process orchestrator không mất workflow.

Asynchronous checkout — Đưa payment status và secondary effect sau broker giúp bound request latency và cô lập dependency. User giờ cần contract `PENDING` trung thực, còn operator phải sở hữu backlog age, replay, DLQ và workflow có thể incomplete nhiều giờ.

Compensation không phải rollback — Release inventory, cancel order hay refund payment là business action mới có thể fail sau khi action gốc đã external-visible. Mỗi compensation cần idempotency, legal precondition, audit record và reconciliation fallback riêng.

Outbox guarantee — Local database change và outbox row atomic, nhưng publish có thể lặp và consumer có thể crash sau side effect. Stable event id, aggregate sequence check cùng inbox/effect uniqueness là chi phí lâu dài đổi lấy reliability.

Database per service — Ownership và failure isolation tốt hơn, nhưng join, report và cross-domain consistency biến thành asynchronous product. Không cho Saga update table của service khác; dựng analytics từ event/CDC thay vì cross-service request-time join.

Adoption order — Tune query/index và pool, cô lập browse khỏi checkout, thêm CDN/cache cùng async secondary effect, rồi partition consumer và chỉ shard/cell về sau. Mỗi bước cần triggering metric, owner, rollback và failure drill; nếu không architecture chỉ có thể phình ra.
Invariant nào có thể break?

Oversell, capture trùng và order báo confirmed trong khi stock/payment bất đồng là các failure quan trọng. Inventory conditional update, một provider idempotency key và legal versioned transition trong từng service authoritative bảo vệ chúng; Saga chỉ điều phối, không phải source of truth của participant state.
Metric nào detect sớm nhất?

Theo dõi tỷ lệ checkout accepted/completed và p99 cùng oldest non-terminal Saga age, outbox age, consumer lag, reserve-conflict rate, tuổi PSP `UNKNOWN` và reconciliation mismatch. Queue depth một mình che mất partition bị kẹt.
Blast radius được contain thế nào?

Dùng gateway route, pool, concurrency budget và bounded queue riêng cho browse, cart, checkout, PSP và after-payment lane. Partition theo order/SKU khi cần, cap một campaign hoặc hot SKU tại admission và cho secondary consumer lag mà không ăn checkout capacity.
Retry có duplicate hoặc reorder work không?

Mặc định là có. Bind client key với canonical request hash và original response, tái dùng cùng provider key, cấp stable id plus aggregate version cho mỗi command/event, rồi apply consumer effect trong local transaction kèm inbox hoặc unique business key.
Repair và prove recovery thế nào?

Reconcile Saga row quá tuổi với Order, Inventory, Payment và PSP; replay committed outbox; repair bằng transition confirm, release, cancel hoặc refund tường minh; sau đó redrive quarantined event. Chứng minh recovery bằng zero unmatched capture/reservation, outbox/consumer age có giới hạn và aggregate sequence check theo mẫu.
Reserve atomic + ghi outbox
Conditional update là oversell guard cuối; outbox commit cùng reservation.
Inbox dedupe + optimistic fence cho Saga
At-least-once delivery là mặc định; inbox key và version predicate làm replay vô hại.
Replay event stream vào index mới
Replay là công cụ rebuild, không phải shortcut correctness: consumer vẫn cần idempotent effect và version check.
Chạy Kafka local, rồi dừng consumer khi rebuild lag về zero.
Tìm payment attempt cần reconcile
UNKNOWN là state durable. Query provider trước khi quyết định capture, refund hoặc retry.

A supplied e-commerce architecture claims 1M DAU and a 10x promotion, while the shared planning tiers are 1M and 10M requests/day. Normalize the workload, then evolve CDN, gateway, search, cart and a checkout Saga from 1M to 10M without premature service or database sharding. Which lane scales first, and how do local outboxes preserve order, inventory and payment correctness?

**Normalize the unit first:** DAU is a population, not traffic. Write the assumptions explicitly: `requests/day = DAU × journeys/user/day × API calls/journey`; then split the result by browse, cart and checkout. Under the shared planning factor, 1M requests/day is about 250 rps peak and 10M/day about 2,500 rps peak. A 10x promotion is a burst with a duration and hot-SKU skew, not automatically a new daily tier. **Physical shape at 1M:** Keep the boxes as logical ownership boundaries. A modular monolith or a few coarse services may share one HA relational cluster while using separate schemas, transactions and connection pools. Put static assets on the CDN, let search read a rebuildable index/cache, keep Cart DB durable with Redis as acceleration, and isolate the checkout pool from browse traffic. **Adoption order toward 10M:** Fix query/index shape and pool waits; add CDN/cache plus request coalescing; scale gateway, search and cart horizontally; bound checkout admission by the measured inventory/PSP drain rate; then partition event consumers by order or SKU. Shard only when write/data volume, restore time or blast radius—not the headline rate—becomes binding. **A service-local reservation plus outbox transaction:** 
BEGIN;
--
INSERT INTO command_inbox(command_id, request_hash, status)
VALUES (:command_id, :request_hash, 'PROCESSING')
ON CONFLICT (command_id) DO NOTHING;
-- if row_count = 0: stop and return the stored outcome
--
UPDATE inventory
SET available = available - :qty, version = version + 1
WHERE sku_id = :sku_id
  AND available >= :qty
  AND version = :expected_version;
-- require row_count = 1, otherwise roll back as SOLD_OUT/CONFLICT
--
INSERT INTO reservation(id, sku_id, order_id, qty, state, expires_at)
VALUES (:reservation_id, :sku_id, :order_id, :qty, 'HELD', :expires_at);
--

Asynchronous delivery and replay
Moving work off the request path trades immediate failure for lag, duplicates, ordering constraints and operational backlog.
Define delivery semantics
Assume at-least-once at service boundaries. Give each event a stable ID, partition key, schema version and event time; make every side effect idempotent.
Guarantee order only within the business entity that needs it. Global order limits parallelism and usually encodes no useful invariant.
Treat lag as user impact
Observe oldest-message age, input/output rate, retry count, poison messages and partition skew. Queue depth alone hides slow old work behind new small messages.
Use retry topics or delayed queues with expiry and a DLQ; DLQ is not resolution until it has ownership, alerting and a safe replay tool.
Evolve safely
Use backward/forward-compatible schemas and tolerant readers. Deploy consumers before producers when adding fields and preserve raw events for bounded replay.
Replay into an isolated output or shadow consumer first; throttle it so historical traffic cannot starve live processing or repeat external effects.

Caching as a bounded copy
A cache is a disposable, stale copy with a failure mode. Its key, TTL and origin-protection plan are part of correctness.
Choose what may be stale
Include tenant, authorization dimension and schema version in keys. Never cache a security or monetary decision unless the product defines acceptable staleness.
Use cache-aside for simple reads, versioned keys for safe rollout and randomized TTLs to avoid synchronized expiry; cap negative-cache lifetime.
Protect the origin
Coalesce concurrent misses, refresh hot values ahead of expiry and bound rebuild concurrency. A cache outage must not instantly multiply origin load by the hit ratio.
Monitor hit ratio by key class, eviction, memory fragmentation, hot keys, fill latency and origin amplification—not only cache latency.
Compare tiers
L1 removes a network hop but multiplies stale copies; shared L2 centralizes data and invalidation but adds a network dependency and hotspot risk.
Choose LRU/LFU/TTL from access distribution and object value. If eviction loses authoritative state, the component is a database wearing a cache label.

Reliability, overload and recovery
Reliability is a user-visible contract. Capacity, retries and failover must be designed as bounded control loops rather than emergency switches.
Prevent positive feedback
Give every call an end-to-end deadline; derive shorter per-hop timeouts from the remaining budget and cancel work the caller no longer needs.

Degrade deliberately
Use admission control, bounded queues, concurrency limits and load shedding before saturation; queue depth without oldest-age is not enough to see stalled work.
Define which features fail closed, fail open, serve stale data or become read-only. Test the degraded contract with dependency latency, partial-region loss and bad configuration.
Prove recovery
Set RTO and RPO per journey, automate restore/failover where safe, and regularly restore production-shaped backups into an isolated environment.
Roll out by canary or cell, compare user SLIs, and keep rollback independent of the failing control plane. A failover plan that has never been exercised is an assumption.
